Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the program. I'm Professor Hill. I know your reading list is long, so here is my best advice. Don't read every article from the first page to the last. That is the slowest way to read. Start with the abstract. It is the shortest part, and often the most useful. Then skim the conclusion. Ask yourself: is this article important for my question? If it is, read it more carefully. The methods section is usually the most difficult part, so read it last. And please, choose peer-reviewed articles. They are more reliable than blogs or news websites.

Hi, I'm Anna. I'm doing my PhD in marketing in the Netherlands, and I read in English every day. In my first year I used a translator for everything. It was faster, of course. But after six months my English was not better. I didn't learn the words, so every new article was just as difficult. In my second year I changed my method. I read the abstract in English, with no translator. I write down the five most important words, and I only translate a paragraph when it is really necessary. It is slower at the beginning, but now I read much faster than before, and my vocabulary is bigger.
